land.text: Palmyra and the Roman East that Odaenathus held after the defeat at Edessa: 'ruled Syria' under a nominal Roman framework, 'from the Pontic coast in the north to Palestine in the south' (Odaenathus page)

predecessors.note: The infobox gives 'Established: 260 as a kingdom; 270 as an empire'. The roman-empire dossier dates the Roman loss of the East to 267; the Odaenathus page treats him as 'effectively independent within a nominal Roman framework' from 260 (notes).

land.text: Palmyra, garrisoned in 272 and razed in 273 after the revolt of Septimius Apsaios; the rest of the empire returned to Aurelian in 272

successors.note: Cliopatria's row ends in 269, four years before the page's end.

capitals.name: Palmyra
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Palmyra'; 'Named after its capital city, Palmyra'. The infobox's largest city is Alexandria.

rulers.name: Odaenathus
rulers.title: king (ras of Palmyra from the 240s)
rulers.note: Assumed 'the title of king' in 260 after the Roman defeat at Edessa; killed with his son Herodianus in late 267 (266 or 268 also proposed). The King of Kings title is placed in 263 without contemporary evidence.

rulers.name: Vaballathus
rulers.note: Aged ten at his accession under Zenobia's regency; the infobox gives 267/270-272; Augustus in late 271.

rulers.name: Zenobia
rulers.title: regent, then co-ruler
rulers.note: Regent for Vaballathus from 267; the infobox lists her as ruler 272-273, which does not fit the narrative, and her fate after the capture near the Euphrates in 272 is uncertain.

rulers.name: Antiochus
rulers.title: Augustus (proclaimed in the revolt)
rulers.note: A relative of Zenobia, declared Augustus in the 273 revolt under Septimius Apsaios and spared by Aurelian when Palmyra was razed.

correction.text: Syria, cleared of the Persians in late summer 260 ('struck the retreating Persian army between Samosata and Zeugma and drove Shapur I out of Syria')

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria begins in 261, but the page has Odaenathus take the title of king in 260 and, in late summer 260, drive Shapur I out of Syria. Syria alone is drawn for 260.

correction.text: Syria, Phoenice and Palaestina, held after the defeat of Quietus and Macrianus at Emesa in 261; for 261 only

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's 261-262 shape (0.94 M km2; bbox 23.4-40.6 N, 27.7-40.6 E) reaches Egypt (23.4 N) and western Anatolia (27.7 E). The page puts Egypt in 270 (Palmyrene Empire page) and Galatia in 271, and in 261 Odaenathus 'sided with Gallienus' and the Emesans killed Quietus as he approached Emesa. 261 is drawn as Syria, Phoenice and Palaestina ('from the Pontic coast in the north to Palestine in the south' is undated); 262 is the next keyframe. Neither page gives an infobox area.

correction.text: Syria, Phoenice, Palaestina and, from spring 262, Osroene with Edessa, Carrhae and Nisibis

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 262: 'In spring 262 he recaptured Edessa and Carrhae and regained Nisibis'; the campaign 'fully restored Osroene and Mesopotamia' (northern Mesopotamia, not the Tigris plain: the Ctesiphon siege failed).

union.text: Anatolia's eastern region (read as Cappadocia): 'By 263, Odaenathus was in effective control of the Levant, Roman Mesopotamia and Anatolia's eastern region'

correction.text: the 262 shape unchanged for 263-264: Syria, Phoenice, Palaestina and Osroene plus Cappadocia, Anatolia's eastern region held 'by 263' (Odaenathus page)

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's 263-264 shape (1.04 M km2) is the maximum extent of 271 (Egypt, western Anatolia) drawn eight years early. The Odaenathus page has the Persian wars of 262-263 end outside Ctesiphon with Osroene and Mesopotamia restored, and Egypt is never named in his territory. [fx-42, 2 Nov 2026: Cappadocia added (R034); without it the snap would take Odaenathus's eastern Anatolia away again.]

union.text: Anatolia's eastern region (read as Cappadocia): 'By 263, Odaenathus was in effective control of the Levant, Roman Mesopotamia and Anatolia's eastern region'

correction.text: the 262 shape unchanged for 265-269: Syria, Phoenice, Palaestina and Osroene; Vaballathus under Zenobia's regency from 267 plus Cappadocia, Anatolia's eastern region held 'by 263' (Odaenathus page)

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's 265-269 shape (1.04 M km2) again includes Egypt and Anatolia. For 265-269 the Odaenathus page gives the same territory as 262-263 (second Persian invasion 266-267, Odaenathus killed in late 267, Zenobia securing the Persian border and the Tanukhids in Hauran); the 270 spring and autumn conquests follow. [fx-42, 2 Nov 2026: Cappadocia added (R034); without it the snap would take Odaenathus's eastern Anatolia away again.]

union.text: Anatolia's eastern region (read as Cappadocia): 'By 263, Odaenathus was in effective control of the Levant, Roman Mesopotamia and Anatolia's eastern region'

correction.text: Syria, Phoenice, Palaestina, Osroene, Roman Arabia (Bosra, Jordan) and Egypt, the latter from October-November 270 plus Cappadocia, Anatolia's eastern region held 'by 263' (Odaenathus page)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 270, the year of the empire: spring, Roman Arabia after the sack of Bosra; October-November, 'Zenobia is declared queen of Egypt'. Egypt is drawn as the Nile valley and Delta (the Cliopatria shape is not the whole country). [fx-42, 2 Nov 2026: Cappadocia added (R034); without it the snap would take Odaenathus's eastern Anatolia away again.]

union.text: Anatolia's eastern region (read as Cappadocia): 'By 263, Odaenathus was in effective control of the Levant, Roman Mesopotamia and Anatolia's eastern region'

correction.text: Syria, Phoenice, Palaestina, Osroene, Arabia, the Nile valley and Delta, and Galatia with Ancyra: 'the greatest extent of the Palmyrene expansion' plus Cappadocia, Anatolia's eastern region held 'by 263' (Odaenathus page)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 271, 'the greatest extent': 'The Palmyrenes subdue Galatia and occupy Ancyra'; attempts on Chalcedon failed. The page's 'large parts of Asia Minor' is undated beyond Galatia and not drawn. The shape comes to about 0.49 M km2 (gazetteer cells) against Cliopatria's 1.04 M km2, a ratio near 0.47, because Cliopatria's shape covers the whole of Egypt south to 23.5 N and western Anatolia. [fx-42, 2 Nov 2026: Cappadocia added (R034); without it the snap would take Odaenathus's eastern Anatolia away again.]

correction.text: Palmyra and its neighbourhood, besieged in the summer of 272; the provinces are Aurelian's

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 272: Aurelian crosses the Bosphorus, wins at Immae and Emesa, takes Antioch and besieges Palmyra in the summer; only Palmyra and its steppe remain until the siege ends.

correction.text: the city of Palmyra in revolt, razed by Aurelian in 273

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 273: 'Palmyra rebelled under the leadership of a citizen named Septimius Apsaios', proclaimed Antiochus Augustus, and Aurelian 'spared Antiochus, but razed Palmyra'.

region.text: Palmyra, where Odaenathus 'assumed the title of king' after the Roman defeat at Edessa

ledger.note: 260: Odaenathus becomes king of Palmyra. Valerian 'was defeated near Edessa in late spring 260 and taken prisoner'; the page has him assume 'the title of king' that year; the Palmyrene Empire infobox: 'Established: 260 as a kingdom; 270 as an empire'. He keeps nominal loyalty to Gallienus and 'minted coins only in Gallienus's name'.

region.text: Syria, from which Shapur I was driven in late summer 260

ledger.note: 260: Odaenathus clears Syria. 'In late summer 260, Odaenathus struck the retreating Persian army between Samosata and Zeugma and drove Shapur I out of Syria.' The page gives the year and the land; that Palmyra then held it is the reading.

region.text: Syria, Phoenice and Palaestina: his authority ran 'from the Pontic coast in the north to Palestine in the south'

ledger.note: 261: Odaenathus rules the Roman East. He sided with Gallienus and 'the Emesans killed Quietus as Odaenathus approached the city' in early 261; the page lists Syria, Phoenice, Palaestina, Arabia and the eastern parts of Anatolia as his territory without a year (page silent), so the extent is bridged here. The roman-empire dossier dates the same loss to 267. [fx-42: the Odaenathus page dates eastern Anatolia 'By 263'; see ledger/5.]

region.text: Edessa and Carrhae recaptured and Nisibis regained in spring 262; Osroene and Mesopotamia restored

ledger.note: 262: northern Mesopotamia returns. 'In spring 262 he recaptured Edessa and Carrhae and regained Nisibis, which he sacked'; the campaign 'fully restored Osroene and Mesopotamia'.

region.text: Osroene and the road to Ctesiphon, outside which he stood 'by late 262 or early 263'

ledger.note: 262: Odaenathus carries the war to the Persians. After retaking Nisibis he reached Ctesiphon in late 262 or early 263; the siege failed.

region.text: Anatolia's eastern region (read as Cappadocia): 'By 263, Odaenathus was in effective control of the Levant, Roman Mesopotamia and Anatolia's eastern region'

ledger.note: By 263: eastern Anatolia is Odaenathus's. Odaenathus page: 'By 263, Odaenathus was in effective control of the Levant, Roman Mesopotamia and Anatolia's eastern region' and his authority covered 'Anatolia's eastern regions and, following the campaign of 262, Osroene and Mesopotamia', 'from the Pontic coast in the north to Palestine in the south'. The page names no province: Cappadocia is the reading (the Persians 'ravaged Cappadocia and Cilicia' in 260 and Odaenathus fought raiders in Bithynia in 266-267, neither shown as his land). Galatia is not taken here: the Palmyrene Empire page has the Asia Minor operations begin 'In 271' with 'The Palmyrenes subdued Galatia, and occupied Ancyra' (ledger/10). roman-empire ledger/96 gives Rome's 267 loss as 'Syria, Palestine and large parts of Asia Minor' (Cilicia, Galatia, Cappadocia); only the eastern part is supported before 271. [Added fx-42, 2 Nov 2026, for the dossier request R034.]

region.text: Osroene and the road to Ctesiphon

ledger.note: 267: the Persian war ends with Odaenathus. A second invasion in 266 reached Ctesiphon, he 'broke off the siege to face Germanic raiders' in Anatolia, and he was assassinated in late 267; the page records no treaty, so the year is bridged from his death. Zenobia then worked at 'guaranteeing the safety of the borders with Persia' (Palmyrene Empire page).
270: the Palmyrene kingdom becomes an empire. Infobox: 'Established: 260 as a kingdom; 270 as an empire'; Vaballathus is ruler from 'Rulers: Vaballathus (267/270-272)'.

region.text: Roman Arabia: in spring 270 Zabbai and Zabdas 'sack Bosra, kill the Roman governor, and secure Roman Arabia'

ledger.note: spring 270: Roman Arabia falls. Zenobia's expedition against the Tanukhids ends with the sack of Bosra and the governor's death.

region.text: Egypt: 'A Palmyrene army of 70,000 invaded Egypt, and Zenobia is declared queen of Egypt'

ledger.note: October-November 270: Egypt. The Roman general Tenagino Probus 'retakes Alexandria in November but is defeated, besieged at Babylon Fortress'; Zabdas then secures Egypt. The Claudius Gothicus page has the Palmyrene army move into Egypt 'in the late summer' of its 269 narrative, and the roman-empire dossier dates it to late 271 from the Crisis of the Third Century page (not opened here); the Palmyrene Empire page, the state's own article, is followed.
spring 271: Galatia. Zabbai began operations in Asia Minor and Zabdas joined him in spring; 'The Palmyrenes subdue Galatia and occupy Ancyra, the empire's greatest extent'; Chalcedon was not taken.

region.text: Syria, Phoenice, Palaestina and Arabia: Zenobia 'retreated to Antioch then fled to Emesa while Aurelian advanced and took the former', after Immae

ledger.note: 272: Aurelian retakes the East. He is said to have crossed the Bosphorus in 272, defeated Zenobia at Immae, taken Antioch and beaten her again at Emesa 'forcing her to evacuate to the capital'; the page gives no date to the battles inside the year.

region.text: Galatia and Ancyra, regained as Aurelian advanced through Anatolia and reached Tyana; Cappadocia too, where Tyana lies

ledger.note: 272: Anatolia returns. 'Aurelian to that point had destroyed every city that resisted him, but he spared Tyana.' [fx-42: Cappadocia added with the 263 gain (ledger/5).]

region.text: Egypt: 'According to one account, Marcus Aurelius Probus regained Egypt from Palmyra'

ledger.note: 272: Egypt returns. 'All other accounts indicate that a military action was not necessary', because Zenobia had pulled back to defend Syria; the year is the page's section, not a dated sentence.

region.text: Palmyra after the summer siege: Zenobia 'captured near the Euphrates and brought back to the emperor'; defenses destroyed

ledger.note: summer 272: Aurelian besieges Palmyra. 'Aurelian besieged Palmyra in the summer of 272'; Zenobia fled east for Persian help and was captured near the Euphrates; the city capitulated and was garrisoned. Palmyra stays on the map in 273 for the revolt.
273: Palmyra rebels under Septimius Apsaios, proclaims Antiochus Augustus, and Aurelian 'spared Antiochus, but razed Palmyra'; the infobox 'Disestablished: 273'. The page gives no month.

wars.name: Odaenathus against Macrianus and Quietus
wars.outcome: Odaenathus sided with Gallienus; the Emesans killed Quietus as he approached in early 261 and Balista was captured and executed in autumn 261; Syria stayed under Odaenathus.
wars.note: The page places Macrianus's defeat in the Balkans in spring 261, which conflicts with its own timeline. No border moved.

wars.name: Odaenathus's Persian wars
wars.outcome: After driving Shapur I out of Syria in late summer 260 he retook Edessa, Carrhae and Nisibis in spring 262, besieged Ctesiphon in late 262 or early 263 and again in 266 and broke off to face Germanic raiders; Gallienus took the title Persicus maximus after 263.
wars.note: No treaty is recorded; the war ended with Odaenathus's assassination in late 267.

wars.name: Palmyrene conquests of Arabia, Egypt and Galatia
wars.outcome: Zenobia's generals took Roman Arabia (Bosra), Egypt (Probus defeated at Babylon Fortress) and Galatia; Chalcedon held out.

wars.name: Aurelian's reconquest of the Palmyrene Empire
wars.outcome: Aurelian crossed the Bosphorus, beat Zenobia at Immae and Emesa, took Antioch, besieged Palmyra in the summer of 272 and razed it in 273 after the revolt under Septimius Apsaios.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey lines; the extents are provinces named without boundaries, and the Anatolian edge is undated beyond Galatia.

notes:
Cliopatria's three Palmyrene shapes (261-262, 263-264, 265-269; 0.94-1.04 M km2) all reach Egypt (to 23.5 N) and western Anatolia (to 27.7 E), the extent of 271, and stop in 269, four years before the page's end in 273; all three are marked wrong and replaced by dated keyframes. Disagreements: Egypt dated October-November 270 (Palmyrene Empire page), late summer in the 269 narrative (Claudius Gothicus page) or late 271 (the roman-empire dossier, from the Crisis of the Third Century page, not opened here); the roman-empire dossier also dates the Roman loss of the East to 267, where the Odaenathus page has him effectively independent from 260 ('something between powerful subject, independent vassal king and rival emperor'); Cilicia and Cappadocia, listed lost in that dossier, are not mentioned under Zenobia by the Palmyrene Empire page. The page gives no infobox area. Vaballathus's and Zenobia's rule years follow the infobox; Zenobia's fate is uncertain. Page budget (1-2) exceeded by one, the Odaenathus page being needed for 260-267. A gap-filler could open Zenobia, Battle of Immae and Battle of Emesa (272) for months and the Anatolian extent. The Kingdom of Kush appears among Cliopatria's neighbours in 261-269 only because Cliopatria's Palmyrene shape runs to Aswan; no page opened has contact.
Fix pass fx-42 (2 Nov 2026), dossier request R034: ledger/5 (263) and the 263, 265, 270 and 271 keyframes now hold Cappadocia (312 cells) as the 'eastern region' of Anatolia that the Odaenathus page puts under Odaenathus 'By 263'; ledger/12 (272) returns it with Galatia. Galatia and Cilicia stay out until 271 (Palmyrene Empire page: Asia Minor operations 'In 271'), so roman-empire ledger/96 (267: Cilicia, Galatia, Cappadocia) is still wider than this dossier; handoff written.
